subject: IAC orchestration + networking checklist for on-prem/private deployment
messages:

Subject: On-prem deployment: Terraform/Helm/Ansible review and network constraints

Hannah / team,

Thanks again for taking this on. We're starting preflight for our private deployment next week and want a focused review of the IaC artifacts before we hand off to our ops team. High level asks:
- Confirm Terraform modules and remote state approach for on-prem (we cannot use public S3).
- Validate Helm chart values that enable private registry pulls and imagePullSecrets.
- Review Ansible playbooks for idempotence and secrets handling (we will use HashiCorp Vault behind a firewall).
- Network constraints: GW routes, egress proxy, and any required NAT/firewall changes.

I've attached the initial artifacts (redwood_onprem_terraform.tf, helm chart bundle, ansible playbook) and a network diagram. Raj from our SI will join the call if needed.

Can you confirm a time for a 60-minute walkthrough and a short checklist you want us to fill out prior to the meeting?

Thanks,
Amanda
Amanda Roy
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Corp

Attachments: redwood_onprem_terraform.tf (tf), helm_chart_redwood_v1.2.tgz (tarball), ansible_playbook_deploy.yml (yaml), network_diagram_v2.png (png)

Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: On-prem deployment: Terraform/Helm/Ansible review and network constraints — initial notes

Team,

I've done a first pass on the Terraform and the ask list below. Key items and recommendations:

- Remote state: since Acme is on-prem, recommend a self-hosted Terraform state backend: Consul or an on-prem object store (minio) behind ACLs. Avoid local state on the CI runner. Add locking via Consul/etcd to prevent concurrent apply.

- Secrets: use Vault agent + Kubernetes CSI driver for secrets. Do NOT bake secrets into Helm values. Ansible playbook should pull short-lived Vault tokens and not commit vault creds to inventory.

- Modules: the redwood_onprem_terraform.tf is a single-file drop. Suggest splitting into modules: (1) network (vlan/subnet/routing), (2) infra (bastion, registry proxy), (3) cluster (k8s nodes, storage class). That will make selective applies safer during upgrades.

- Helm: add values for imagePullPolicy: IfAcmePrivateRegistry, and include registry mirror/proxy config. chart should support an override for registryPullSecret name.

- CI/CD: gate terraform plan with a lint step + automated drift detection. Keep terraform apply locked to a specific service account with MFA on the operator side. We should add a pipeline job that runs terraform validate and a k8s dry-run (helm template + kubectl apply --server-dry-run). Include link to INFRA-9421 for pipeline template.

Small snippet example (for vault integration) in Ansible tasks: 
---
- name: fetch vault token
  uri:
    url: "https://vault.internal.vpc/v1/auth/token/lookup-self"

I'll compile these into a short checklist and share before the Wednesday network review.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: On-prem deployment: Terraform/Helm/Ansible review and network constraints — network & security notes

Quick security/network notes from my pass: 

- Segmentation: enforce at least three segments: management (bastion/API access), control-plane, and workload. Use host-based firewall + infra ACLs.
- Egress: Acme must confirm whether egress is allowed to public Docker registries. If not, we need an internal registry mirror and a NAT/egress proxy. Add proof-of-concept instructions in the helm values (imageRegistry.mirror).
- DNS and service discovery: recommend internal DNS entries for vault, registry, and image mirror. Helm chart should support external-dns overrides.
- Routing: confirm BGP or static route preference. If BGP, ensure route propagation is limited to expected prefixes.
- Audit & logging: ensure the playbook instruments fluent-bit to forward to Acme's logging cluster (or provide a logging endpoint).

Action items for the Friday walkthrough: 
1) Confirm remote-state backend choice (Consul vs MinIO).
2) Validate Vault auth flow (AppRole vs OIDC).
3) Agree on registry mirror and image policies.
4) Decide on CI gating (strict vs permissive for canary).

I'll bring a short network diagram with annotated ACLs. Amanda — can you add the cluster CIDRs (pod/service ranges) to the drive folder before the meeting?

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Security & Compliance Lead

Amanda / team,

Thanks for the quick turn. From Acme's side we'll commit to providing the cluster CIDRs and the private registry FQDN by EOD Wednesday. Proposed canary scope (for Friday's test):
- Deploy core control-plane components (helm chart core), no data plane workloads.
- Validate registry pull via mirror and Vault-based secret injection.
- Run terraform apply for network + registry proxy in a sandbox VLAN only.

If the above passes, we expand to the worker nodes next week and ramp to the full cluster. Please confirm whether CI will require manual approval for terraform apply in sandbox or we should allow a service account with time-limited creds.

I'll join the Friday walkthrough remotely; Amanda will run the calendar invite.

— Raj
